meg.title: meg- prefix
meg.explanation: The most common preverb by far, and the odd one out — it doesn't add a direction, it changes ASPECT. Attached to a verb, it turns an ongoing or generic action into a single, completed event: eszik ("to eat", ongoing) becomes megeszik ("to eat up", a finished act of eating). This is the single most important preverb to get a feel for, since it changes what KIND of action a verb describes, not just where it points.

el.title: el- prefix
el.explanation: Motion away — departure, leaving. With some verbs it also marks completion, the way meg- does (elolvas, "to read through").

example.en: I'm going off to the shop.

ki.title: ki- prefix
ki.explanation: Motion outward, out of an enclosed space — the mirror image of be-. Often pairs with a noun in the elative case (-ból/-ből, "out of").

example.en: I'm going out of the room.

be.title: be- prefix
be.explanation: Motion inward, into an enclosed space — the mirror image of ki-. Often pairs with a noun in the illative case (-ba/-be, "into").

le.title: le- prefix
le.explanation: Downward motion — the mirror image of fel-/föl-.

fel.title: fel- prefix
fel.explanation: Upward motion — the mirror image of le-. Also shows up in idioms for "getting up" or "picking something up" (felkel, "to get up out of bed"). föl- is a real dialectal variant with the exact same meaning, not a different preverb — both are correct.

example.en: I get up in the morning.

föl.title: föl- prefix
föl.explanation: Identical in meaning to fel- ("up") — a regional/dialectal variant, more common in some speakers' everyday Hungarian, not a separate or "wrong" form. The two are interchangeable in essentially every context.

át.title: át- prefix
át.explanation: Crossing motion — across or through something, from one side to the other.

rá.title: rá- prefix
rá.explanation: Motion onto something's surface. Often pairs with a noun in the sublative case (-ra/-re, "onto") when the destination is named.

example.en: I put it onto the table.

vissza.title: vissza- prefix
vissza.explanation: Returning motion — going back, or undoing a previous action.

össze.title: össze- prefix
össze.explanation: Combining or gathering things together. With some verbs it extends the other way — things coming apart under pressure (összetörik, "to shatter/break into pieces", from törik "to break") — the shared thread is several things ending up interacting with each other, not a specific direction.

elő.title: elő- prefix
elő.explanation: Bringing something forward or ahead — presenting, producing, or moving to the front.

után.title: után- prefix
után.explanation: Following after someone or something, in time or in space.

ide.title: ide- prefix
ide.explanation: Motion toward HERE — the speaker's own location. Paired with oda- ("there"), this is one of the few preverb pairs defined by the speaker's position rather than a fixed direction.

oda.title: oda- prefix
oda.explanation: Motion toward THERE — somewhere away from the speaker. Paired with ide- ("here"); which one applies depends on where the speaker is standing, not on the verb itself.
